name: CloudTAK-Plugin_StatusBoard_CAP
description: Replaced CAP ILWG's shared Status Board Google Sheet with a live, multi-user, CoT-aware mission status board in CloudTAK. Single canonical store with computed views; syncs with WMIRS via two data paths (live scrape + cached SQLite).
highlight: Eliminated manual VLOOKUP coordination across 10+ operators during active sorties.

name: CloudTAK-Plugin-CAP-C3
description: 10-tab Command & Control panel for CAP Emergency Services in CloudTAK. Covers member tracking, sortie management, resource log, task assignment, and CoT integration — all in a single reactive store.
highlight: Consolidated 10 separate tracking workflows into one panel for CAP ES commanders.

name: WMIRS-Auth
description: FastAPI backend that proxies WMIRS (CAP's ASP.NET mission management system) via authenticated session scraping. EServices login + TOTP 2FA, full mission/sortie/resource normalization, SQLite sync, background polling, and CoT output to TAK Server.
highlight: Bridges a closed, screen-scrape-only government system into a live REST API + TAK CoT feed for the whole IL Wing.

name: ILWG-WMIRS
description: Next.js 14 App Router frontend for the WMIRS-Auth backend. Gives Illinois Wing operators a web interface to mission data pulled live from WMIRS — missions, sorties, resources, and unit log.
highlight: A proper web UI over WMIRS data that ILWG operators can actually navigate — no more raw ASP.NET screens.

name: VISTA
description: Live video streaming infrastructure for ILWG CAP. Flask relay server, MediaMTX restreamer, and WebTAK plugin integration for RTSP/RTSPS/SRT/RTMP streams. Ground truth for the WebTAK Video Viewer and Channels plugins.
highlight: Illinois Wing's operational video-over-TAK stack — cameras on the common operating picture.

name: WebTAK-Plugin-Channels
description: Channel and group management plugin for WebTAK in the ILWG CAP / VISTA stack. Browse, join, and manage TAK channels directly from the WebTAK map interface.
highlight: Brings multi-channel coordination to WebTAK dispatchers during ILWG activations.

name: WebTAK-Plugin-VideoViewer
description: Floating, resizable video windows for RTSP/RTSPS/SRT/RTMP/HLS feeds layered over the WebTAK map. Routes all streams through TAK Restreamer (MediaMTX) as HLS or WebRTC WHEP. Built for the ILWG CAP / VISTA stack.
highlight: Live camera feeds from MediaMTX directly overlaid on the WebTAK common operating picture.

name: CloudTAK-Plugin_RoutePlanner_CAP
description: Route planning plugin for CloudTAK tailored to CAP Emergency Services operations. Builds and shares mission routes across the TAK network for ground and air sorties.
highlight: Mission route planning integrated directly into the CloudTAK COP for CAP ES.

name: ATAK-Plugin-QuickCapture
description: Quick feature capture and sync to ArcGIS feature services from ATAK. QR-code project templates, photo attachments, CalTopo integration, and bidirectional ArcGIS sync with offline support.
highlight: Field teams capture and upload geo-features directly to ArcGIS with no desktop workflow.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-FeatureLink
description: Bidirectional bridge between Esri ArcGIS Feature Services and the TAK ecosystem. Pushes CoT to ArcGIS feature layers, writes PLI tracks back from feature layers to TAK. Full platform coverage: ATAK 5.6/5.7, WinTAK 5.6/5.7, CloudTAK, and TAK Portal.
highlight: One feature service, visible and editable from ATAK, WinTAK, CloudTAK, and ArcGIS simultaneously — no manual sync.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-Aleph
description: Draw a search area on any TAK client and receive an offline data package (imagery, DTED elevation, OSM street data) back as a mission package. Python service handles tile fetching and package assembly; ATAK, WinTAK, CloudTAK, and infra-TAK clients included.
highlight: Pre-loaded offline map tiles for a mission AO in one draw operation — no GIS desk or desktop tool required.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-EsriDashboard
description: Esri Operations Dashboard-style analytics and situational awareness panels for ATAK, WinTAK, and CloudTAK. Displays live feature-layer data, PLI tracks, and unit status from ArcGIS alongside the TAK common operating picture.
highlight: Brings Esri's dashboard analytics into the TAK COP — no second screen or separate GIS client needed.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-CrowdCAD
description: Crowd-sourced CAD bridge + ATAK/CloudTAK/WinTAK/WebTAK clients for event dispatch. Built for IU football medical operations — responders on ATAK, dispatchers on WinTAK and CloudTAK, CoT-linked.
highlight: Operational at IU home games — ATAK-equipped medical responders dispatched live from the TAK COP.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-IndianaUniversity
description: TAK plugin suite for Indiana University football game medical operations. ATAK responders receive dispatch calls from WinTAK/CloudTAK dispatchers. IU-branded unit templates, responder position markers, and CoT dispatch flow.
highlight: ATAK-equipped IU medical responders dispatched from a TAK COP at home games — real operational deployment.

name: TAK-Plugin-UI-Builder
description: Drag-and-drop visual designer for ATAK plugin layouts. Generates valid Java/XML for DropDownReceiver dialogs and panels. No build step — deployed as a static GitHub Pages app.
highlight: Live at jpat-12.github.io/TAK-Plugin-UI-Builder — zero-install dev tool for the TAK community.

name: ATAK-Plugin_ICU
description: ATAK 5.6 plugin reverse-engineered from ICU and uastool APKs. Turns an Android phone into a UAS ground control station integrated with the TAK common operating picture.
highlight: Bridges phone-as-UAS-platform into the TAK COP without proprietary hardware or vendor lock-in.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-ICU_VideoStreamer
description: Camera-to-map video streaming plugin suite for ATAK and WinTAK. CoT-linked video overlay and media server integration — puts live camera feeds directly on the TAK common operating picture.
highlight: Live video overlaid on the TAK map, synchronized with CoT markers — both ATAK and WinTAK.

name: WinTAK-ICU
description: Windows desktop application for camera-to-map video streaming integrated with the TAK common operating picture. .NET 8, FFmpeg, LibVLC — brings phone-based ICU video streaming to WinTAK operators.
highlight: Ports phone-based UAV video streaming to the Windows TAK client — same CoT markers, desktop form factor.

name: ATAK-Plugin_TAK-Portal
description: ATAK plugin for signing in to TAK Portal via Authentik SSO and installing plugins from the portal's ProductProvider catalog. Bearer token forwarded through reverse proxy.
highlight: Closes the loop between TAK Portal plugin distribution and in-field ATAK installs — scan and install from the map.

name: InfraTAK-Plugin-TAKRestreamerQRCodes
description: infra-TAK plugin that generates QR codes for TAK Restreamer (MediaMTX) stream endpoints. Scan to connect field devices to live streams without typing URLs.
highlight: One QR scan puts a field device on the right MediaMTX stream path — no URL memorization.

name: InfraTAK-Module-MigrateAuthentik
description: infra-TAK module for migrating Authentik SSO configurations between versions or instances. Automates the transition of authentication flows, users, groups, and applications.
highlight: Automates the painful Authentik migration process for TAK infrastructure operators upgrading SSO stacks.

name: InfraTAK-Plugin-Aleph
description: infra-TAK companion plugin for the Aleph offline data package workflow. Provides the server-side tile-fetch service and package assembly UI within the infra-TAK management console.
highlight: Offline map package generation accessible straight from the TAK infrastructure admin panel.

name: TeamAwearnessKit-Esri-Integration
description: Early Node-RED bridge connecting Survey123 form submissions to CoT markers on TAK, and CoT position tracks back to ArcGIS Online feature layers. The bidirectional Esri ↔ TAK closed loop that preceded FeatureLink.
highlight: Proved the Survey123 → TAK → ArcGIS closed loop before the full FeatureLink suite existed.

name: z_survey123-cot
description: Node-RED-based converter that transforms ArcGIS Survey123 form submissions into Cursor on Target (CoT) messages, sending submitted locations and attributes as map markers on the TAK network in real time.
highlight: Field survey data appears as CoT markers on TAK as soon as the form is submitted — no manual re-entry.

name: ATAK-Plugin_OpenAtlas
description: ATAK plugin integrating OpenAtlas map data into the TAK common operating picture. Extends the basemap with community-contributed geographic context and feature data.
highlight: Community atlas data on the TAK COP — context beyond standard tile basemaps.

name: TAK-Repeater
description: Python UDP relay for TAK CoT traffic. Bridges TAK networks across segments or repeats CoT messages to multiple endpoints — useful for extending SA range or logging CoT streams.
highlight: Extends TAK network SA coverage without additional TAK Server infrastructure.

name: TAK Tracker
description: Python-based CoT track logging utility for TAK networks. Captures and processes PLI position reports for analysis, archiving, or relay to secondary systems.
highlight: Lightweight CoT track logging outside the TAK Server stack — runs anywhere Python does.

name: TAKServer-Automation
description: ATAK-compatible Android utility for automating TAK Server administrative tasks from the field — user provisioning, certificate management, and server configuration without a browser or SSH session.
highlight: TAK Server admin from ATAK in the field — user certs and accounts without touching a laptop.
